edits.english: A dilemma was raised before the Sages: When one brings a burnt offering, which atones for violations of positive mitzvot, does a burnt offering atone even for a violation of a positive mitzva that its owner committed after designating the animal as an offering, or does it not atone for such a violation?

As Rashi noted, this is not referring to an offering that was slaughtered not for its sake, but to a more general question concerning a burnt offering. Although the Sages derived from the verses that bringing this offering is atonement for neglecting positive mitzvot, there is no Torah obligation to bring a burnt offering for a specific transgression (and there is a reason for this, as not only can a person violate many positive mitzvot at every passing moment, without measure, but also in this type of mitzvot, a person cannot know what he has transgressed and to what extent he has transgressed). However, on the other hand, since this offering has an aspect of atonement, it is possible to learn the laws of atonement from the sin offering, for which the Torah gave specific laws. It is also logical that only a transgression for which the offering was designated and consecrated is atoned for by the burnt offering.
